# Load packages & set variables

```{r}
#| label: load packages
#| message: false # removes tidyverse loader & here location for privacy
#| warning: false

library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(ggthemes)
library(zoo)
library(DT)

source(here("functions", "set_env-variables.R"))
source(file.path(PATH_FUNCTIONS, "load_functions.R"))
```

# Load merged dataset & drop unusable pid's & years

```{r}
#| label: load df & drop unusable

sparse_df <- load_clean_df("merged") # called sparse cause i didnt fill anything yet

n_before <- sparse_df %>%
  pull(pid) %>%
  unique() %>%
  length()

# I drop all pid's that never responded to the phq4 questions, as i dont have a depvar to work with for those cases
sparse_df <- sparse_df %>%
  group_by(pid) %>%
  filter(any(!is.na(depression_phq4_score_in_1y))) %>%
  ungroup()

# I also drop all years before 2013 as 2016 was the first measure of phq4, so 2013 is the first year where the "depressive score in 3 years" value can have entries. I keep 2 years beforehand for now tho to extrapolate to 2013 if necessary
sparse_df <- sparse_df %>% filter(syear >= 2011)

# Lastly, I drop all entries where death_year < syear, this can happen cause they sometimes obtain death-specific data
sparse_df <- sparse_df %>%
  filter((is.na(death_year) |
    death_year >= syear))


n_after <- sparse_df %>%
  pull(pid) %>%
  unique() %>%
  length()
print(
  paste(
    "Nr. of PID's remaining: ",
    n_after,
    ", corresponding to ",
    round(n_after / n_before * 100, 2),
    "% of all pid's.",
    sep = ""
  )
)

rm(n_before, n_after)
```

# Depressive Prevalence Testing

```{r}
#| label: prevalence table

sparse_df %>%
  drop_na(depression_phq4_binary_in_1y) %>%
  # count & prepare
  count(syear,
    depression_phq4_binary_in_1y,
    wt = weight
  ) %>%
  group_by(syear) %>%
  mutate(
    prevalence = n / sum(n),
    prevalence = scales::percent(prevalence, accuracy = 0.01)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(syear = syear + 1) %>% # to print the actual years of depression
  filter(depression_phq4_binary_in_1y) %>%
  select("Year" = syear, "Prevalence" = prevalence) %>%
  export_return(
    "02_depression_prevalence_year",
    caption = "Reports the percentage of individuals displaying depressive symptoms above the PHQ-2 threshold in the given year.",
    label = "depression_prevalence_year",
    tabular.environment = "tabular",
    align = c("l", "r"),
    digits = c(0, 0, 2)
  )
```

# drop variables

## too little data available

all variables with \<= 1 year of observations starting at 2015 are dropped, as there is too little data to extrapolate from. "Insights" generated by reconstructed and imputed versions of these variables are likely to be artifacts of the techniques applied.

```{r}
#| label: drop too little data

# detect variables with >= 1 year of data beginning at 2015
vars_no_data <- sparse_df %>%
  select(pid, syear, age:last_col()) %>% # only consider predictor candidates
  filter(syear >= 2015) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), as.character)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(pid, syear),
    names_to = "variable",
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  group_by(syear, variable) %>%
  summarise(
    any_non_na = any(!is.na(value)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  group_by(variable) %>%
  summarize(drop = if_else(sum(any_non_na) < 2, TRUE, FALSE)) %>%
  filter(drop == TRUE) %>%
  pull(variable)

sparse_df <- sparse_df %>%
  select(-all_of(vars_no_data))
```

## irrelevant / inferior variables

- death_year: all dead people have been excluded
- born_germany_parents: collinearity with migback: none -\> TRUE here, direct & indirect -\> FALSE here
- born_germany: collinearity with migback: none & indirect -\> TRUE here, direct -\> FALSE here
- job_changed: information preserved in job_nr_individual

```{r}
#| label: drop irrelevant

sparse_df <- sparse_df %>%
  select(-c(
    born_germany_parents,
    born_germany,
    death_year,
    job_changed
  ))
```

# Fill grouping variables

## housing moved in year

critical to do first, as it allows grouping by person and dwelling (important for filling variables such as "how big is your flat" from other years in the same dwelling)

### procedure: fill if identical

get all move years, for each value fill upwards, then fill with first syear of person

1.  get all move years, ex 2012 and 2016
2.  for a missing value, fill in the highest move year that isnt higher than syear
3.  for all where syear \<= min, create arbitrary value (min(syear) for example) to group by

### apply procedure

```{r}
#| label: fill housing moved

# apply procedure:
moved_df <- sparse_df %>%
  group_by(pid) %>%
  # fill upwards
  arrange(pid, syear) %>%
  mutate(housing_temp = housing_moved_in_year) %>%
  fill(housing_temp, .direction = "up") %>%
  mutate(housing_moved_in_year = if_else(
    housing_temp <= syear,
    housing_temp,
    housing_moved_in_year
  )) %>%
  select(-housing_temp) %>%
  # fill all trailing na's with last move &
  # fill all na's in middle with latest move at that point
  fill(housing_moved_in_year, .direction = "down") %>%
  # only remaining NA are now leading na's -> replace with min(syear) to obtain a valid grouping for them (this variable is not used in the analysis later so this value could also be any arbitrary value)
  mutate(housing_moved_in_year = if_else(
    is.na(housing_moved_in_year),
    min(syear),
    housing_moved_in_year
  )) %>%
  ungroup()

print_missingness_reduction(moved_df, sparse_df)
```

## job nr individual/household

### procedure: fill downward & summarize

some pid-syear combinations are present in the "base" df (ppathl, intended as base for joining), but not in the individual-level datasets. this can occur if no personal interview was conducted but household variables were still gathered (person usually isnt the head of the household in that case). This is the case for `r round(nrow(moved_df %>% filter(is.na(data_personal))) / nrow(moved_df) * 100, 2)`% of all pid/syear combinations present in the dataset.

This can be fixed by filling downwards. This carries the same assumptions as before: we only increment job_nr if job_changed is true, it remains the same for NA and FALSE. Thus, we assume that job changes are indicated, if not in the missing year, then in the following one.

household job nr can be computed by sum(job_nr_individual) grouped by hid, syear.

### apply procedure

```{r}
#| label: fill job nr

# do individual job nr.
job_nr_df <- moved_df %>%
  group_by(pid) %>%
  arrange(pid, syear) %>%
  fill(job_nr_individual, .direction = "down") %>%
  ungroup()

job_nr_df <- job_nr_df %>%
  left_join(
    job_nr_df %>%
      # create join df that only contains the household variable & joins
      select(hid, syear, job_nr_individual) %>%
      group_by(hid, syear) %>%
      # increases by 1 every time someone in household changes job
      summarize(temp = sum(job_nr_individual, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
      group_by(hid) %>%
      # normalization, not really necessary, but ensures job_nr_household always starts at 1
      mutate(temp = temp - min(temp, na.rm = TRUE) + 1),
    by = join_by(hid, syear)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    job_nr_household = if_else(!is.na(hid),
      temp,
      NA
    ),
    temp = NULL
  )


print_missingness_reduction(job_nr_df, moved_df) %>% print()
```

# Fill regular variables

## stable variables

### procedure: fill with mode

these variables are fixed within their grouping.

### variables

+---------------+----------------------+
| Dependent on  | Variables            |
+===============+======================+
| pid           | height_m             |
+---------------+----------------------+
| pid + house   | neighbourhood_type\  |
|               | housing_east_west\   |
|               | distance_city_centre |
+---------------+----------------------+
| pid + job     | occupation_position  |
+---------------+----------------------+

### apply procedure

```{r}
#| label: fill stable

# apply procedure:
stable_df <- job_nr_df %>%
  arrange(pid, syear) %>%
  # grouped by person
  group_by(pid) %>%
  mutate(height_m = mode(height_m, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # grouped by person and dwelling
  group_by(pid, housing_moved_in_year) %>%
  mutate(
    neighbourhood_type = mode(neighbourhood_type, na.rm = TRUE),
    housing_east_west = mode(housing_east_west, na.rm = TRUE),
    distance_city_centre = mode(distance_city_centre, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # grouped by person and job of the person
  group_by(pid, job_nr_individual) %>%
  mutate(occupation_position = mode(occupation_position, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()

print_missingness_reduction(stable_df, job_nr_df)
```

## variables stable over short periods

### procedure: impute last known variable with limit

these variables are not expected to exhibit frequent changes. thus, they are filled downwards for 2 years max.

### variables

+---------------+------------------+
| Dependent on  | Variables        |
+===============+==================+
| pid           | chronic_illness\ |
|               | character\_      |
+---------------+------------------+
| pid + house   | housing_status   |
+---------------+------------------+
| pid + hid     | housing_carework |
+---------------+------------------+

### apply procedure

```{r}
#| label: fill stable over short periods

# apply procedure:
short_df <- stable_df %>%
  arrange(pid, syear) %>%
  # grouped by person
  group_by(pid) %>%
  fill_n(chronic_illness, character_optimism, character_rumination, character_irritable, character_nervous, character_worrying,
    .direction = "down", .n = 2, .time = "syear"
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # grouped by person and dwelling
  group_by(pid, housing_moved_in_year) %>%
  fill_n(housing_status,
    .direction = "down", .n = 2, .time = "syear"
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # grouped by person and household number
  group_by(pid, hid) %>%
  fill_n(household_carework,
    .direction = "down", .n = 2, .time = "syear"
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

print_missingness_reduction(short_df, stable_df)
```

## ordinal, unidirectional

### procedure: impute last known value

education_level can only ever increase, meaning last years value is the minimum it can be.

### variables

+---------------+------------------+
| Dependent on  | Variables        |
+===============+==================+
| pid           | education_level\ |
|               | stroke_ever      |
+---------------+------------------+
| pid + house   |                  |
+---------------+------------------+
| pid + job     |                  |
+---------------+------------------+

### apply procedure

```{r}
#| label: fill unidirectional

# apply procedure:
unidirectional_df <- short_df %>%
  arrange(pid, syear) %>%
  # grouped by person
  group_by(pid) %>%
  fill(education_level, stroke_ever, .direction = "down") %>%
  ungroup()

print_missingness_reduction(unidirectional_df, short_df)
```

## continuous, major jumps unlikely

### procedure: linear interpolation

these variables tend have high inertia and progress slowly, if at all.

### variables

+---------------+-----------------------+
| Dependent on  | Variables             |
+===============+=======================+
| pid           | hobbies_hours_weekly\ |
|               | sleep_hours_weekly\   |
|               | weight_kg\            |
|               | disability_degree     |
+---------------+-----------------------+
| pid + house   |                       |
+---------------+-----------------------+
| pid + job     | income_net\           |
|               | overtime_hours_month  |
+---------------+-----------------------+

### apply procedure

```{r}
#| label: fill continuous

# apply procedure:
continuous_df <- unidirectional_df %>%
  arrange(pid, syear) %>%
  # grouped by person
  group_by(pid) %>%
  mutate(
    hobbies_hours_weekly = hobbies_hours_weekly %>%
      na.approx(x = syear, na.rm = FALSE),
    sleep_hours_weekly = sleep_hours_weekly %>%
      na.approx(x = syear, na.rm = FALSE),
    weight_kg = weight_kg %>%
      na.approx(x = syear, na.rm = FALSE),
    disability_degree = disability_degree %>%
      na.approx(x = syear, na.rm = FALSE)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # grouped by person and job of the person
  group_by(pid, job_nr_individual) %>%
  mutate(
    income_net_individual = income_net_individual %>%
      na.approx(x = syear, na.rm = FALSE),
    overtime_hours_month = overtime_hours_month %>%
      na.approx(x = syear, na.rm = FALSE)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # grouped by person and household jobs
  group_by(pid, job_nr_household) %>%
  mutate(income_net_household = income_net_household %>%
    na.approx(x = syear, na.rm = FALSE)) %>%
  ungroup()

print_missingness_reduction(continuous_df, unidirectional_df)
```

## likert scales, major jumps unlikely

### procedure: linear interpolation with rounding

these variables tend have high inertia and progress slowly, if at all. rounding is done to preserve scale

### variables

+---------------+----------------------+
| Dependent on  | Variables            |
+===============+======================+
| pid           | sleep_quality\       |
|               | health_description\  |
|               | health_satisfaction\ |
|               | life_satisfaction\   |
|               | eval_self_positive\  |
|               | stress_deal_well\    |
|               | feels\_\             |
|               | belief\_             |
+---------------+----------------------+
| pid + house   | neighbourhood\_      |
+---------------+----------------------+
| pid + job     | income_satisfied\    |
|               | job_satisfaction     |
+---------------+----------------------+

### apply procedure

```{r}
#| label: fill likert

# apply procedure:
likert_df <- continuous_df %>%
  arrange(pid, syear) %>%
  # grouped by person
  group_by(pid) %>%
  mutate(
    sleep_quality = sleep_quality %>%
      interpolate_likert(time_col = syear),
    health_description = health_description %>%
      interpolate_likert(time_col = syear),
    health_satisfaction = health_satisfaction %>%
      interpolate_likert(time_col = syear),
    life_satisfaction = life_satisfaction %>%
      interpolate_likert(time_col = syear),
    eval_self_positive = eval_self_positive %>%
      interpolate_likert(time_col = syear),
    stress_deal_well = stress_deal_well %>%
      interpolate_likert(time_col = syear),
    feels_lonely = feels_lonely %>%
      interpolate_likert(time_col = syear),
    feels_left_out = feels_left_out %>%
      interpolate_likert(time_col = syear),
    feels_isolated = feels_isolated %>%
      interpolate_likert(time_col = syear),
    belief_others_control_life = belief_others_control_life %>%
      interpolate_likert(time_col = syear),
    belief_self_shapes_destiny = belief_self_shapes_destiny %>%
      interpolate_likert(time_col = syear),
    belief_little_control_life = belief_little_control_life %>%
      interpolate_likert(time_col = syear)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # grouped by person and dwelling
  group_by(pid, housing_moved_in_year) %>%
  mutate(
    neighbourhood_pollution_noise = neighbourhood_pollution_noise %>%
      interpolate_likert(time_col = syear),
    neighbourhood_pollution_air = neighbourhood_pollution_air %>%
      interpolate_likert(time_col = syear),
    neighbourhood_greenspace_insufficient = neighbourhood_greenspace_insufficient %>%
      interpolate_likert(time_col = syear),
    neighbourhood_cohesion = neighbourhood_cohesion %>%
      interpolate_likert(time_col = syear),
    neighbourhood_feel_safe = neighbourhood_feel_safe %>%
      interpolate_likert(time_col = syear)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # grouped by person and job of the person
  group_by(pid, job_nr_individual) %>%
  mutate(
    income_satisfied_individual = income_satisfied_individual %>%
      interpolate_likert(time_col = syear),
    job_satisfaction = job_satisfaction %>%
      interpolate_likert(time_col = syear)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # grouped by person and household jobs
  group_by(pid, job_nr_household) %>%
  mutate(income_satisfied_household = income_satisfied_household %>%
    interpolate_likert(time_col = syear)) %>%
  ungroup()

print_missingness_reduction(continuous_df, unidirectional_df)
```

## non-numeric, major jumps unlikely

### procedure: fill if surrounding values are identical

these variables measure behaviour and attitudes. these variables tend have high inertia and progress slowly, if at all.

### variables

+---------------+-------------------+
| Dependent on  | Variables         |
+===============+===================+
| pid           | friends_frequency |
+---------------+-------------------+
| pid + house   |                   |
+---------------+-------------------+
| pid + job     | overtime_ever\    |
|               | work_nights       |
+---------------+-------------------+

### apply procedure

```{r}
#| label: fill ordinal

# apply procedure:
ordinal_df <- likert_df %>%
  arrange(pid, syear) %>%
  # grouped by person
  group_by(pid) %>%
  fill_if_constant(friends_frequency) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # grouped by person and job of the person
  group_by(pid, job_nr_individual) %>%
  fill_if_constant(overtime_ever, work_nights) %>%
  ungroup()

print_missingness_reduction(ordinal_df, likert_df)
```

## non-numeric, major jumps unlikely, cyclical measure

### procedure: copy to off-cycle years, then fill if identical

cyclical measure means its reasonable to use last cycle-year value. these variables measure behaviours and attitudes. these variables tend have high inertia and progress slowly, if at all.

### variables

+---------------+--------------------+
| Dependent on  | Variables          |
+===============+====================+
| pid           | sports_frequency\  |
|               | smoker\            |
|               | alcohol_frequency\ |
|               | sleep_disorder     |
+---------------+--------------------+
| pid + house   |                    |
+---------------+--------------------+
| pid + job     |                    |
+---------------+--------------------+

### apply procedure

```{r}
#| label: fill biannually measured

# apply procedure:
biannual_df <- ordinal_df %>%
  arrange(pid, syear) %>%
  # grouped by person
  group_by(pid) %>%
  fill_n(sports_frequency, smoker, sleep_disorder, .n = 1, .time = "syear") %>%
  fill_n(alcohol_frequency, .n = 3, .time = "syear") %>%
  fill_if_constant(sports_frequency, smoker, sleep_disorder, alcohol_frequency) %>%
  ungroup()

print_missingness_reduction(biannual_df, ordinal_df)
```

## constructed variables

### procedure:

recalculate with same formulas as in 01_merging-datasets

|              | obese       |
+--------------+-------------+

+--------------+-------------+

### apply procedure

```{r}
#| label: fill constructed

# apply procedure:
constructed_df <- biannual_df %>%
  arrange(pid, syear) %>%
  # grouped by person
  group_by(pid) %>%
  mutate(
    bmi = (weight_kg) / (height_m^2),

print_missingness_reduction(constructed_df, biannual_df)
```

## interdependent variables

### procedure:

for groups with structural missingness, establish logical fill. If value cannot be constructed from other variables, establish dummy for models to recognize as interaction effect.

### variables

+-----------------------------+------------------------------------+
| Dependent on                | Variables                          |
+=============================+====================================+
| pid                         |                                    |
+-----------------------------+------------------------------------+
| pid + house                 |                                    |
+-----------------------------+------------------------------------+
| pid + job                   |                                    |
+-----------------------------+------------------------------------+
| pid + occupation            | job_satisfaction\                  |
|                             | overtime_ever\                     |
|                             | overtime_hours_month               |
+-----------------------------+------------------------------------+

### job_satisfaction

```{r}
#| label: job_satisfaction missingness visualization
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 10

{
  occupation_position_table <- table(constructed_df$occupation_position, useNA = "always")
  occupation_position_vector <- paste(
    names(occupation_position_table),
    " (n = ",
    as.vector(occupation_position_table),
    ")",
    sep = ""
  )
  names(occupation_position_vector) <- names(occupation_position_table)
  rm(occupation_position_table)
}

constructed_df %>%
  count(occupation_position, job_satisfaction) %>%
  group_by(occupation_position) %>%
  mutate(n = n / sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    isna = ifelse(is.na(job_satisfaction), TRUE, FALSE),
    label = if_else(isna, n * 100, NA) %>% round(digits = 2),
    label = if_else(isna, paste(label, "%", sep = ""), NA),
    label_y = if_else(isna, if_else(n > 0.5, n - 0.075, n + 0.075), NA)
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(
    x = factor(job_satisfaction),
    y = n,
    fill = !isna,
    label = label
  )) +
  facet_wrap(~occupation_position,
    labeller = labeller(occupation_position = occupation_position_vector),
    scales = "free_x"
  ) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_label(fill = "white", mapping = aes(y = label_y), hjust = 1, size = 3) +
  theme_minimal() +
  fill_qualitative() +
  guides(fill = "none") +
  guides(color = "none") +
  labs(
    x = "Job Satisfaction",
    y = "Percent of Respondents",
    title = "Job Satisfaction per Occupation Position",
    subtitle = "Highlighting Missingness",
    caption = ""
  ) -
  partial(export_return, filename = "02_job-satisfaction-na_occupation", width = 10, height = 10)
```

Missingness is concentrated to certain groups, including pensioners, unemployed people, people pursuing higher education and people doing community service. These groups do not have traditional jobs, meaning a job_satisfaction value is not meaningful for them. Thus, I introduce a missingness indicator for these groups and fill with a dummy value (-1) to ensure they are kept in the dataset without enabling biases. I do not change any existing values, and instead assume that some pensioners still do minijobs or similar.

### overtime_ever

```{r}
#| label: overtime_ever vs overtime_hours_month

constructed_df %>%
  count(overtime_ever, overtime_hours_month) %>%
  mutate(hours = factor(
    if_else(overtime_hours_month == 0, "0", ">0"),
    levels = c("0", ">0")
  )) %>%
  group_by(overtime_ever, hours) %>%
  summarize(n = sum(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(overtime_ever) %>%
  mutate(n = n / sum(n) * 100) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = hours, y = n, fill = hours)) +
  facet_wrap(~overtime_ever) +
  geom_col() +
  theme_minimal() +
  fill_qualitative() +
  guides(fill = "none") +
  guides(color = "none") +
  labs(
    x = "Overtime hours last month",
    y = "Percent of Respondents in Group",
    title = "Overtime last month by self-reported 'have you ever worked overtime'",
    subtitle = "Grouped by '0 hours last month' or 'more than 0 hours last month'"
  ) -
  partial(export_return,
    filename = "02_overtime-month-na_occupation",
    width = 10,
    height = 10
  )
```

As expected, people who reported to have never worked overtime also responded that they have not worked overtime in the last month. Notably, a group with recorded and/or imputed hours of overtime but no response to overtime_ever exists, meaning these values can be filled. Additionally, a similar picture to above emerges:

```{r}
#| label: overtime_ever by group
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 10

constructed_df %>%
  count(occupation_position, overtime_ever) %>%
  group_by(occupation_position) %>%
  mutate(n = n / sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    isna = ifelse(is.na(overtime_ever), TRUE, FALSE),
    label = if_else(isna, n * 100, NA) %>% round(digits = 2),
    label = if_else(isna, paste(label, "%", sep = ""), NA)
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(
    x = factor(overtime_ever),
    y = n,
    fill = !isna,
    label = label
  )) +
  facet_wrap(~occupation_position,
    labeller = labeller(occupation_position = occupation_position_vector),
    scales = "free_x"
  ) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_label(fill = "white", size = 3) +
  theme_minimal() +
  fill_qualitative() +
  guides(fill = "none") +
  guides(color = "none") +
  labs(
    x = "Overtime",
    y = "Percent of Respondents",
    title = "Overtime per Occupation Position",
    subtitle = "Highlighting Missingness",
    caption = ""
  ) -
  partial(export_return, filename = "02_overtime-ever-na_occupation", width = 10, height = 10)
```

Same situation as before: The concept of overtime is not meaningful for groups that are not in traditional employment, including self- and un-employed people, people pursuing education and pensioners. Thus, in addition to "if overtime_ever is NA but overtime_hours is not, impute", the procedure outlined for job_satisfaction will also be applied for the relevant groups.

### apply procedure

```{r}
#| label: fill interdependent

# apply procedure:
interdependent_df <- constructed_df %>%
  arrange(pid, syear) %>%
  # impute overtime_ever based on overtime_hours_month:
  # only edit if a) overtime-ever is NA, b) overtime_hours_month is not na, then do ifelse based on overtime_hours_month > 0
  mutate(overtime_ever = if_else(
    is.na(overtime_ever),
    if_else(
      !is.na(overtime_hours_month),
      if_else(overtime_hours_month > 0, TRUE, FALSE),
      overtime_ever
    ),
    overtime_ever
  )) %>%
  # apply group-based filling for job_satisfaction, overtime_ever and overtime_hours_month
  group_by(pid) %>%
  mutate(
    job_satisfaction = if_else(
      is.na(job_satisfaction) &
        occupation_position %in% c(
          "education/training",
          "not employed",
          "retired",
          "military/community service"
        ),
      -1,
      job_satisfaction
    ),
    overtime_ever = if_else(
      is.na(overtime_ever) &
        occupation_position %in% c(
          "education/training",
          "self-employed",
          "not employed",
          "retired",
          "military/community service"
        ),
      -1,
      overtime_ever
    ),
    overtime_hours_month = if_else(
      is.na(overtime_hours_month) &
        occupation_position %in% c(
          "education/training",
          "self-employed",
          "not employed",
          "retired",
          "military/community service"
        ),
      -1,
      overtime_hours_month
    )
  ) %>%
  # add indicators
  mutate(
    job_satisfaction_meaningful = if_else(job_satisfaction == -1, FALSE, TRUE),
    overtime_meaningful = if_else(overtime_ever == -1, FALSE, TRUE)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

print_missingness_reduction(interdependent_df, constructed_df, strict_column_match = FALSE)
```

# drop impute-only years

2011 and 2012 were only kept to act as impute data for 2013 and onwards, thus dropped now. technically, 2023 could be dropped here, as we have no depression data from future years. kept for potential sanity checks

```{r}
#| label: drop impute-only years

reconstructed_df <- interdependent_df %>%
  filter(syear >= 2013)
```

```{r}
) %>%

    label = "na-reduction_reconstruction_full",
```


The 2 variables missing compared to the full table are "job_nr_individual" and "housing_east_west". Reason is that within the "only include those rows with value in depression_in_1y" filter these variables are already at 0% missingness in sparse df.
